events.quote: The Committee also reviewed easyJet’s undrawn facility arrangements and approved management’s recommendation to enter into a new Revolving Credit Facility for $1.7 billion. This new facility replaced the previous $1.75 billion UKEF facility and the $400 million Revolving Credit Facility, both of which have now been terminated.
events.summary: easyJet entered into a new revolving credit facility that replaced its previous UK Export Finance facility and smaller revolving credit facility, both terminated, lowering annual interest charges.
events.title: New revolving credit facility replaces prior facilities

events.quote: In the year, easyJet repaid a €500 million Eurobond, and secured a $1.7 billion revolving credit facility (RCF) which is undrawn at 30 September 2025 (this new RCF replaced an existing $400 million RCF and a $1,750 million
events.summary: easyJet repaid a Eurobond on its maturity date and secured a new undrawn revolving credit facility.
events.title: Eurobond repaid at maturity

events.quote: Right of use asset disposals in note 18 includes £73 million (2024: £nil) relating to the purchase of eight aircraft that were previously leased, with a corresponding £237 million (2024: £nil) of additions to aircraft owned assets. The early exit of the leases and subsequent purchase of the aircraft resulted in a £54 million (2024: £nil) credit to the income statement.
events.summary: easyJet bought aircraft it had previously leased, exiting the leases early and recording a credit to the income statement.
events.title: Purchase of previously leased aircraft

events.quote: Building on this profit growth, easyJet continues to have one of the strongest investment grade balance sheets in European Aviation (Baa2/stable from Moody’s and BBB+/stable from Standard & Poor’s).
events.summary: easyJet held investment grade corporate credit ratings from Moody's and Standard & Poor's, both with stable outlooks.
events.title: Investment grade ratings affirmed

events.quote: During the year the Committee reviewed and recommended to the Board the refresh of the Company’s EMTN Programme, which had originally been established in January 2016. The refresh of the EMTN Programme allows easyJet to access a diverse range of funding alternatives.
events.summary: The Committee reviewed and recommended a refresh of the Company's Euro Medium Term Note programme to access a diverse range of funding alternatives.
events.title: EMTN programme refreshed

events.quote: Airline net financing charges increased due to reduced interest income from lower market interest rates on our cash and an increase in interest charges relating to borrowings.
events.summary: Airline net financing charges rose due to lower interest income on cash and higher interest charges on borrowings.
events.title: Airline financing charges increased
